newsitem.title: USA: Productivity rose 2.6 percent in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Productivity rose 2.6 percent in first quarter.

text.p: U.S. productivity rose in the first quarter at the quickest pace in more than three years, allowing American workers to enjoy their biggest gain in pay and benefits in five years, the Labour Department said Wednesday.
Productivity outside the farm sector rose a revised 2.6 percent last month after a 1.3 percent gain in the fourth quarter of 1996.

The first-quarter rise previously was reported as 2.0 percent. It was the largest since a 2.6 percent increase in the fourth quarter of 1993 and was last exceeded by a 5.9 percent increase in the fourth quarter of 1992.
Large gains in productivity allow businesses to boost output without raising costs, a crucial factor in containing inflation.

Hourly compensation, after adjusting for inflation, rose a revised 2.8 percent after a 0.3 percent fourth-quarter rise. The first-quarter gain, previously reported as 2.3 percent, was the largest since a 4.8 percent jump in the first quarter of 1992.
The compensation includes wages and salaries and employer contributions for insurance and private benefit plans.
